clue.text: To withdraw comedian is a gamble

parts.note: to scratch is to withdraw from a race or contest
a card is a joker or wag, a funny person

explanation.surface: Pulling a comic off the bill is a risky move.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery ticket you rub to reveal a prize is a small bet on luck.

clue.text: What a feller does to economise

explanation.surface: A woodcutter's job described as a way of saving money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' is not a man but one who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree-feller brings trees to the ground with an axe, and to reduce spending is to trim expenses.

clue.text: Detaining those left in a circus

indicators.note: the remainder is placed within the arena phrase

parts.note: a circus is a ring, so 'a circus' gives A RING
the rest are those remaining

explanation.surface: Locking up the performers who stayed behind in the big top.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking someone into police custody is holding them.

clue.text: Banter is rubbish

explanation.surface: A remark that teasing talk is worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Light teasing talk is one sense; husks separated from grain, hence worthless stuff, is the other.

clue.text: Prudence gets a formal warning

explanation.surface: A woman named Prudence is officially reprimanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prudence' looks like a woman's name; it is the quality of carefulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefulness in acting is one sense; a police officer's official reprimand without charge is the other.

clue.text: What a sailor climbs on the equator?

definitions.text: What a sailor climbs on the equator?

parts.words: What a sailor climbs on the equator?
parts.note: sailors climb rope rungs in the rigging, and the equator is known at sea as the Line, so this is a rope rung read as a line for a seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor scaling something while crossing the equator.
explanation.definitionFit: These small ropes tied across the shrouds form the ladder steps up a ship's rigging.

clue.text: Container made by Peruvian in Tennessee

indicators.note: the Peruvian is placed within the state abbreviation

parts.note: TN is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Tennessee
the Inca were the native people of Peru

explanation.surface: A receptacle made by a South American living in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal can is a sealed receptacle for food or drink.

clue.text: Just the boat for a vagabond

explanation.surface: Exactly the right vessel for a wandering tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing vessel using drift nets is one sense; an aimless wanderer is the other.

clue.text: A union leader, in Coventry perhaps, displays sharpness

indicators.note: the union's first letter goes within the city

parts.note: Coventry is an example of an English city

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A trade union boss in a Midlands city shows keen wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Keenness of vision or thought is acuteness.

clue.text: Ardent fan always supports church pioneer

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece that supports another sits below it

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
a leader goes first, like a pioneer

explanation.surface: A devoted follower forever backs a religious trailblazer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leads crowd support at games is an enthusiastic supporter.

clue.text: 50 per cent of city firms hold on to big businessmen

indicators.note: half the word, here its latter two letters
the firms enclose the next word

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, so COS are companies

explanation.surface: Half the City's companies are clinging on to wealthy magnates.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnates are wealthy, powerful industrialists.

clue.text: Adequate swimmers take in air

indicators.note: the swimmers enclose the following word

parts.note: fish are creatures that swim

explanation.surface: Swimmers gulp a breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderately good, reasonably satisfactory.

clue.text: He must study church law

parts.note: a cleric of a cathedral chapter shares his title with the body of church rules he must know

explanation.surface: A clergyman's duty to learn ecclesiastical rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral cleric bears the same name as a church decree.

clue.text: Awfully nice rinse? That's not true

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's dreadful tint described as a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Not genuine or sincere, false in feeling.

clue.text: Weird rites said to have been ridiculed

indicators.note: weird means strange, so the letters are put into a strange order

explanation.surface: Odd ceremonies are claimed to have been mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocked through irony or exaggeration.

clue.text: A flare of exceptional brilliance

explanation.surface: A dazzling signal rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured signal flare fired from a pistol is one sense; extremely bright is the other.

clue.text: Another meeting about the wedding

parts.note: re means concerning
a union is a marriage

explanation.surface: A further gathering concerning a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of people coming together again.

clue.text: Roisterous stableman — a real stunner

parts.note: a lad is a stable worker at a racing yard
a dish is an attractive person

explanation.surface: A rowdy groom who is very good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Boisterous and loutish in the manner of young men.

clue.text: In Cuba salary restrictions are essential

indicators.note: the answer is found in the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Pay limits in Cuba are fundamental.
explanation.definitionFit: Forming the base, fundamental.

clue.text: Following defeat I shall order "quieten down!"

indicators.note: the contraction comes after the word for defeat

parts.note: to best is to beat
I'll is the contraction of I shall

explanation.surface: After losing, someone vows to demand silence.
explanation.definitionFit: A command to stay calm and silent.

clue.text: Anything but a short valediction

parts.note: a farewell phrase which, read literally, means very lengthy

explanation.surface: A goodbye that goes on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal goodbye that literally means extremely lengthy.

clue.text: Where many of us meet some of the French?

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, a large number
our means belonging to us
des is French for some, or of the

explanation.surface: A place where crowds gather with some French people.
explanation.walkthrough: The French shrine in the Pyrenees where many pilgrims gather.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrimage town in south-west France is a place.

clue.text: The lady left a key on it maybe

definitions.text: The lady left a key on it maybe

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a lady
F is a musical key

explanation.surface: A woman put her key down somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge on a wall where small objects are placed.

clue.text: Girl takes everyone aback by getting a parrot

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the word for everyone is turned

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A woman shocks everyone by acquiring a talking bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian bird of the parakeet family.

clue.text: Eat around six? Wonderful!

indicators.note: the word for eat goes round the numeral

parts.note: dine means eat
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Dinner at six o'clock, how lovely!
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly, hence superb.

clue.text: Gee! Is no management well-groomed?

indicators.note: management means handling or arranging, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at the lack of smart executives.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegantly and tidily dressed, of a woman.

clue.text: As fraudulent as a bowman may be

explanation.surface: Crooked dealing compared with an archer.
explanation.walkthrough: The bowman is not an archer but a violinist plying his bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaged in cheating is one sense; playing a violin is the other.
